summary: Completed backend API regression + frontend gameplay/integration checks on public URL. Backend core flows passed; frontend has movement-speed regression and a pointer-capture stability risk on touch interactions.

ui_bugs.issue: Observed very low effective movement speed in automation: ~42-45 coords/sec on desktop keyboard (target 270 coords/sec), and ~118 coords/sec on mobile touch hold.
Runtime crash observed when pointer events are malformed/edge-case: Failed to execute 'setPointerCapture' on 'Element': No active pointer with the given id is found.

action_items: Investigate movement performance pipeline (frame timing vs update step vs headless throttling); verify real-browser speed reaches ~270 coords/sec.
Harden setPointerCapture usage in touch handlers (guard/check active pointer id, try/catch fallback) to prevent runtime crash edge cases.
Review Player model mutable defaults (collected/discovered lists) to avoid shared-state side effects in future refactors.
Populate /app/memory/test_credentials.md with any required auth test accounts when non-guest auth expands.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/models.py uses mutable default lists on Player (collected/discovered). Prefer Field(default_factory=list).
Current CORS allowed methods are GET/POST/PATCH only; if future routes add PUT/DELETE, browser requests will fail unless middleware is updated.
seed_data_creation: Created transient guest players/worlds during tests; attempted cleanup via MongoDB teardown in pytest fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite already covers guest/session/profile, world create+duplicate atomic behavior, gating, contribution daily uniqueness, collectibles, and challenge-signature verify/replay. Frontend verified: no horizontal overflow on 1920x800 and 390x844; travel opens same scene (canvas count stable); map territory links open world panel; wallet no-Phantom guidance panel opens. Re-test movement speed and touch pointer-capture fix after patch.
rca of the issue: Movement: consistent low coordinate delta across directions suggests frame/update throughput issue (or automation throttling), not single collision. Pointer crash: UI handlers call setPointerCapture directly on pointerdown in multiple places; if pointer id is not active (edge input path), browser throws and app crashes.
